items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: I just wish that Clarence Teddude's band had recorded, you know.

ctx.x: Well, you see, they played and practiced great music, you know. Oh, yeah. They said, well, when all this jazz came out, they started trying to rag it too.

You know, when the brass band would play for these places where they played for the dance, the brass band would take, like some of them numbers would take the chord of, you know what I mean, the trio, and they played for the dance. Some of them, the trio, some of them brass band, they were so beautiful, you know. They're pretty. Yeah. Well, that's what they do a whole lot of time. But when did the jazz hit over here, the ragtime? Was that around World War I, before or after I won? After. After World War I, it got…
Well, the head was good. The head was called the heeling toe.
